title: Predicted 6 to Actual 7 in IB: A Practical Plan
summary: Turn a predicted IB 6 into a final 7 with a realistic plan for diagnostics, targeted revision, timed practice, feedback, and exam technique.
body_markdown:
A **predicted 6 to actual 7 in IB** is a realistic improvement. It usually requires recovering a relatively small number of marks through better consistency, precision, and exam execution, not relearning the entire course.


Your predicted grade is an evidence-based estimate rather than a limit on what the IB can award. The most effective plan is to calculate your approximate mark gap, identify why marks are being lost, repair those weaknesses, and demonstrate the improvement repeatedly under timed conditions.


### What a predicted 6 actually means


The IB defines a **predicted grade** as a teacher's prediction of the grade a candidate is expected to achieve, based on evidence of the student's work and knowledge of IB standards. Schools may consider mock examinations, class assessments, coursework, consistency, and professional judgment.


Your final subject grade is determined from the marks awarded for official assessment components. Component marks are scaled according to their weightings, combined, and converted into a grade from 1 to 7 using boundaries established for that examination session.


Predicted grade Final IB grade


Estimates your likely performance Records the standard demonstrated in assessed work


Uses evidence available before final examinations Uses completed examinations and coursework


May reflect school assessment practices Follows official weighting, marking, and moderation processes


Can change as your performance develops Is awarded after the assessment session


The official[Diploma Programme grade descriptors](https://ibo.org/contentassets/0b0b7a097ca2498ea50a9e41d9e1d1cf/dp-grade-descriptors-en.pdf) characterize a 7 as excellent performance and a 6 as very good performance. The precise distinction varies by subject, but a 7 generally requires greater consistency, independence, depth, accuracy, and control.


### Calculate the gap between your 6 and a 7


Not every predicted 6 is equally close to a 7. Someone one mark below a recent boundary needs a different plan from a student performing near the bottom of the 6 range.


Collect the following evidence:


- Your latest two or three timed paper scores
- Marks by question, topic, and assessment objective
- Your estimated IA or coursework mark
- Official component weightings for your subject and level
- Recent relevant boundaries, used only as reference points
- Marked scripts and teacher feedback


Estimate your weighted total by multiplying each component percentage by its weighting and adding the results. For example, if examinations are worth 80% and coursework 20%, an examination average of 70% and coursework estimate of 75% produce:

This remains an estimate because boundaries can change. The IB's[student assessment guidance](https://ibo.org/university-admission/discover-why-ib-students-succeed/ib-student-assessment/) explains that grading considers candidate work, grade descriptors, statistical evidence, and examiner judgment.


The[RevisionDojo IB Grade Calculator](https://www.revisiondojo.com/features/grade-calculator) can help organize component marks. Use a range based on several realistic attempts rather than entering only your best score.


### Diagnose why marks are being lost


The difference between a 6 and a 7 is often inconsistent execution. You may understand the syllabus but lose marks through incomplete explanations, weak evaluation, skipped working, imprecise terminology, poor evidence selection, or time pressure.


Review several assessments and classify each lost mark:


Error type Typical problem Best response


Knowledge Missing fact, formula, quotation, or concept Use active recall and spaced repetition


Conceptual Information recalled but not explained or applied Relearn the relationship and practise applications


Method Incorrect process despite knowing the topic Redo worked methods independently


Command term Description given when evaluation was required Plan around the exact instruction


Evidence Insufficient data, examples, textual detail, or working Build and apply compact evidence banks


Accuracy Sign, unit, transcription, or calculation mistakes Use a deliberate checking routine


Timing Rushed or unfinished responses Complete timed sections with decision points


Keep a mistake log containing the question, marks lost, error type, corrected reasoning, and retest date. Every entry should lead to a fresh question that checks whether the weakness has genuinely been corrected.


### Use a targeted revision cycle


Students aiming for a 7 should follow a repeated cycle of **diagnose, repair, practise, and retest** .


### Diagnose under closed-book conditions


Begin with a short exam-style set completed without notes. Mark it strictly so that you distinguish genuine recall from the familiarity created by rereading.


Ask your teacher why an answer missed the highest band, particularly in subjects where marks depend on analysis, evaluation, organization, or evidence. Focus on changes you can reproduce independently.


### Repair the specific weakness


Study only what is needed to fix the diagnosed problem. If equilibrium calculations are weak, do not reread all of Chemistry. If literary analysis lacks discussion of authorial choices, practise connecting technique, effect, meaning, and the question.


Use concise notes, worked examples, flashcards, or Jojo AI to clarify misconceptions. The RevisionDojo guide to[effective IB practice resources](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/effective-ib-practice-resources-ai-study-tools) explains how to progress from explanation to independent application.


### Practise and retest


Complete several questions testing the same skill while gradually removing support. The[RevisionDojo Questionbank](https://www.revisiondojo.com/features/questionbank) can support focused practice by subject, paper, topic, and difficulty.


Attempt each question seriously before checking the solution. Retest the weakness after **48-72 hours** using unfamiliar material. Improvement means transferring the corrected method to a new context, not remembering the previous answer.


### Adapt the plan to your subject


### Mathematics and sciences


Prioritize complete working, notation, units, significant figures where required, and efficient method selection. Practise mixed sets so that you must identify the relevant method without being told the topic.


Redo incorrect solutions from a blank page. Reading a worked answer can feel productive even though the most difficult decision has already been made for you.


### Individuals and societies


Link accurate knowledge directly to the wording of the question. Build compact evidence banks containing examples, data, case studies, perspectives, and limitations, then practise selecting only what supports the argument.


For essays, plan a defensible thesis and the purpose of each paragraph. Evaluation should shape the reasoning throughout rather than appearing as a brief final qualification.


### Languages and literature


Practise close analysis, purposeful organization, accurate terminology, and precise textual reference. Do not merely identify a technique; explain how it shapes meaning, affects an audience, and answers the question.


For language acquisition, combine receptive work with frequent speaking and writing. Track recurring grammar and vocabulary errors, then use the corrected forms in new tasks.


### Protect marks through exam technique


Before answering, identify the **command term** , topic, scope, marks available, required evidence, and approximate time. Official[IB sample examination papers](https://ibo.org/programmes/diploma-programme/assessment-and-exams/sample-exam-papers/) provide verified examples for selected subjects, but confirm that each paper matches your current syllabus and level.


Calculate an approximate pace by dividing working time by total marks. Treat this as guidance, and reserve time to check unanswered subparts, units, labels, calculations, and conclusions.


If you become stuck, record any valid working or relevant reasoning that could earn partial credit, then continue. A 7 is often protected by collecting available marks across the paper rather than perfecting one answer while leaving another unfinished.


### A realistic 6-week improvement plan


Week Main objective Evidence of progress


1 Complete diagnostics and estimate the gap Error profile from two assessments


2 Repair the two highest-cost weaknesses Better accuracy on targeted questions


3 Correct method, structure, and command-term errors Stronger marked responses


4 Complete timed sections Fewer unfinished answers


5 Sit one or two realistic papers Stable scores with detailed review


6 Consolidate errors and protect routine Consistent results on fresh material


A focused session might include 10 minutes of retrieval, 35-50 minutes of targeted questions, and 15-20 minutes of marking and correction. Once a week, replace targeted work with a timed section or full paper. The[RevisionDojo Mock Exams guide](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/revisiondojo-mock-exams) explains how to reproduce realistic conditions and review results effectively.


### Common mistakes to avoid


Do not study every topic equally when only a few weaknesses repeatedly cost marks. Avoid chasing one historical boundary because the boundary for your session is not known in advance. Aim for a sensible buffer across several timed attempts.


Completing papers without reviewing them only measures performance. Memorizing markschemes is also unreliable because it does not guarantee transfer to unfamiliar questions. Treat predicted papers as additional practice, not forecasts of the examination.


Finally, do not sacrifice sleep for extra revision. Rest supports recall, accuracy, and judgment, all of which matter when the difference between grades may be only a few marks.


### Conclusion


Moving from a predicted 6 to an actual 7 requires precise correction rather than unlimited study. Calculate the likely gap, classify lost marks, repair the highest-value weaknesses, and confirm progress through repeated timed work.


RevisionDojo can support this process through the Questionbank, Study Notes, Jojo AI, Grade Calculator, and Mock Exams. Use these tools to make practice targeted, but judge readiness through accurate, independent performance on fresh questions under realistic conditions.
